subject: Private deployment IP manifest and firewall handoff - Acme Health
messages:
From: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@acme-health.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: SecOps <secops@acme-health.com>
Date: Mon, 19 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: private deployment IP manifest & firewall requirements

Hi Marissa,

We're starting the firewall and network design work to onboard Redwood Private into our prod VPC. To complete our compliance packet and to provision rules with the network team we need a concrete, itemized manifest that includes:
- IPs or CIDR blocks we should allow (control plane endpoints, registry/model pull endpoints, telemetry/logging targets)
- Ports and protocols (outbound and any inbound exceptions)
- FQDNs and SNI expectations (do you require SNI match? will you use wildcard certs?)
- Any DNS/TLS or mTLS requirements and certificate pinning details
- Expected behavior for NAT: do you accept a NAT pool or do you require static egress IP(s)?
- Any ephemeral/rotating IPs we should plan for and how often they change

We also have an internal template for allowlist manifests — attaching that for your convenience. Our audit team will want a short written statement we can include in the SOC-guardrails evidence bundle confirming the controls Redwood expects on the customer side.

Target timeline: we'd like to have the final manifest and runbook by EOD next Wednesday (2026-07-28) so the network change window can be scheduled the following week.

Thanks,
Jordan Lee
Networking Lead, Acme Health
Jordan.Lee@acme-health.com

Attachment: acme-allowlist-template.xlsx (XLSX, 18KB)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@acme-health.com>
Cc: SecOps <secops@acme-health.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 19 Jul 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: private deployment IP manifest & firewall requirements

Jordan — thanks for the clear ask and the template. Below is a pragmatic manifest we use for most Private (VPC) deployments; I split it into (A) control plane connectivity and (B) runtime/egress expectations so your networking and security teams can treat them separately for change windows and evidence.

A) Control plane (required outbound from customer VPC to keep the control plane happy)
- DNS: customer must allow outbound DNS (UDP/TCP 53) to their resolver. Redwood control plane FQDNs: control.redwood-inference.com, auth.redwood-inference.com.
- TLS: outbound HTTPS to control.redwood-inference.com on 443. TLS with normal server certs; SNI should be set to control.redwood-inference.com. No client mTLS required for control plane APIs (token-based auth).
- IPs (recommended allowlist for customers that cannot egress via FQDN-only policy): 54.210.128.0/24, 3.120.44.0/23 (note: these are the current egress addresses for our control plane regions; customers should prefer FQDN + cert validation, and treat these IP ranges as fallbacks).
- Ports: 443 outbound for control plane; 443 outbound for model registry pulls. Optional: 80 outbound for health-checks only if you can't do HTTPS interception (discouraged).

B) Runtime and model-serving egress (depends on your deployment mode)
- If you run Redwood runtime in your VPC (private deployment with local runtime):
  - The runtime will only initiate outbound HTTPS to (1) model registry endpoints for initial bootstrap, (2) metrics + logs endpoints if you opt-in to Redwood-managed telemetry, and (3) cloud provider metadata endpoints (IMDS) for autoscaling helper processes.
  - Recommended allowlist for telemetry endpoints: metrics.redwood-inference.com:443, logs.redwood-inference.com:443. If you proxy telemetry through your internal collector, you can block direct egress and point the runtime to the collector.
  - DNS resolution for dynamic model mirrors: customers should allow resolution for the registry hostnames; caching DNS at the resolver is acceptable.

C) NAT/egress guidance
- We support two common models: (1) Static egress IP(s) — provide up to 4 IPs (or a /29) for us to document in your manifest; or (2) NAT pool with known prefix ranges — you must provide the prefix and an approximate rotation window.
- If you provide static IPs we will record them in the runbook and they will be used for control-plane callbacks (where applicable). If you use ephemeral IPs, we require notification to our onboarding mailbox with at least 72 hours lead time prior to rotation for production traffic.

D) Evidence and sign-off language (short blurb you can put in your SOC packet)
- "Redwood Inference has provided a recommended customer-side allowlist manifest and runbook. Acme Health is responsible for implementing outbound firewall rules and NAT configuration documented in the manifest; Redwood has confirmed that required outbound connectivity consists of HTTPS (443) to the control plane FQDNs and/or the documented IP ranges."

E) Attachments and next steps
- Attached: redwood-allowlist-manifest-v1.csv (CSV manifest with columned entries for service, fqdn, ip_or_cidr, ports, protocol, rationale). Also attaching a small runbook snippet with the handshake checklist.
- Action items for Acme:
  1) Confirm whether you will provide static egress IPs or use a NAT pool (reply with IPs or prefix and rotation cadence).
  2) Confirm whether telemetry will be sent to Redwood endpoints or proxied internally.
  3) Confirm your target change window (we recommend a small test window first).

We can also run a 30-minute ops walkthrough (network + security) this week if you want to go line-by-line in the manifest.

Cheers,
Marissa Cole
Sr. Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com

Attachment: redwood-allowlist-manifest-v1.csv (CSV, 3KB)
Attachment: runbook-handshake-snippet.txt (TXT, 1KB)

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@acme-health.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 19 Jul 2026 11:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: private deployment IP manifest & firewall requirements

Adding a couple of implementation notes from the operations side — copying the relevant pieces from our internal playbook. Jordan, feel free to share these with your cloud networking team: 

- If you elect to NAT all outbound traffic through a single static IP, that's the simplest model for firewall rules. Provide that IP and we'll use it as the canonical source for callbacks and troubleshooting.
- If you must use a NAT pool (ephemeral), provide the prefix range and the expected rotation frequency. We'll require a pre-notification process for any rotation that affects production flows.
- DNS: please ensure your resolver does not rewrite or intercept SNI (HTTPS interception) for traffic to control.redwood-inference.com. Our instrumentation and cert expectations depend on unmodified TLS.
- For high-security environments: we can support locking the control plane to the provided static IPs *and* FQDN checks; however, you must accept that we may change the control-plane public IPs during emergency maintenance — such events will be announced and we will push alternate FQDNs.
- Diagram: I attached a simple egress mapping PDF that shows the two patterns (static single-IP NAT vs NAT pool + prefix). That should help the networking folks choose the least amount of churn.

If you prefer, we can produce a short change ticket template for your NOC to submit to the firewall team.

—Laura
Network Reliability, Redwood Inference

Attachment: egress-mapping-diagram.pdf (PDF, 120KB)

Thanks — this is exactly what we needed. A few quick answers and asks from our side: 

1) NAT model: we'll start with a single static egress IP for the pilot. I will follow up with the IP and the ticket number by tomorrow EOB.
2) Telemetry: we'll proxy telemetry through our internal collector (so please point telemetry to the collector host; we will not allow direct egress to metrics.redwood-inference.com).
3) Change window: aiming for the pilot change window on 2026-08-05 so we can run an end-to-end validation on staging first.
4) Evidence: procurement asked for a one-paragraph statement for financial and audit files indicating that Redwood's required customer-side controls are outbound HTTPS to control.redwood-inference.com and the listed IPs. The blurb in your email looks fine — we'll add it to the packet.

Could we schedule the 30-minute ops runbook walkthrough on Thursday 2026-07-22 at 10:00 PT? That would let our networking and compliance teams join. Also copying procurement so they can start the PO paperwork in parallel.

Best,
Jordan
Networking Lead, Acme Health
